id: A Secret Matter of Grave Importance

prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Except when once we drew identical lots nothing’s ever come between us. We keep our drifts of space spare and daily shake our down. You’ve glanced beyond your dirty cuffs and caught me hand-washing my clean shirts. Stuck with sharp wind, both bloods are rare and rarely do we taste the walnut’s knot of oil. We wake between our fitted sheets and shake our fists or pretend real fright but not in this do we dare touch. My rib cage can stand in yours, yours become the swinging doors through which magician’s swords will slice and miss that knotted muscle. It is a trick. We’ll make an endless show of the outright clanking, irregular beating of our acrobatic hearts. We’ve designed the double bars of depth; our hearts skip — the tumbleset we think is absence, the somersault we call forbearance — the hearts are there, doing turns that teach us to count and keep each finger close to its own sly pulse.

Keywords: Except, You, Stuck

outputs.L1: Except for the one time we drew identical lots, nothing has ever come between us. We keep our drifts of space spare and shake our down each day. You have glanced beyond your dirty cuffs and caught me hand-washing my clean shirts. Stung by the sharp wind, both bloods are rare, and rarely do we taste the walnut’s knot of oil. We wake between our fitted sheets and shake our fists, or feign genuine fright, yet even then we do not dare touch. My rib cage can stand within yours; yours can become the swinging doors through which a magician’s swords slice, missing that knotted muscle. It is a trick. We will make an endless show of the outright clanking and irregular beating of our acrobatic hearts. We have designed the double bars of depth; our hearts skip—the tumbleset we mistake for absence, the somersault we call forbearance. The hearts are there, performing turns that teach us to count and to keep each finger close to its own sly pulse.
outputs.L2:
Only once, when chance handed us matching lots, has anything stood between us. We leave our separate stretches of space uncluttered, airing and fluffing our bedding each day. Looking past your stained cuffs, you have seen me scrubbing my spotless shirts by hand. Trapped in a cutting wind, we both carry uncommon blood, and only seldom taste the small, oily knot inside a walnut.

We rise between sheets tailored to us, raising our fists or acting genuinely afraid, yet even here we do not risk contact. My ribs could fit inside yours; yours could turn into swinging doors as a magician’s blades pass through them, narrowly avoiding that tightly bound muscle. The whole thing is an illusion.

We will stage forever the loud, metallic, uneven rhythm of our hearts performing their acrobatics. Together we have built parallel bars over the depths. Our hearts miss a beat—the tumbling sequence we mistake for disappearance, the somersault we name restraint—but they remain, spinning through routines that teach us to count and to hold every finger near its own secretive pulse.
outputs.L3:
The speakers share a close bond that has rarely been broken, even though they deliberately maintain a certain distance from one another. Their contrasting habits and circumstances emphasize their differences, yet they remain connected by identities that are similarly rare, vulnerable, and difficult to sustain. Although they may express anger, fear, or emotional tension, they stop short of genuine physical or emotional contact, as if closeness itself carries an unacceptable risk.

Their intimacy is therefore portrayed as a dangerous illusion. Each person’s body and heart seem to inhabit the other, blurring the boundary between attachment and selfhood. Yet what initially appears to be absence, silence, or restraint is not emptiness. Rather, it is the concealed and irregular movement of two hearts working to preserve their distinct rhythms. Their distance ultimately becomes a way of protecting both their connection and their individuality.
outputs.L4:
The poem explores a relationship defined by intimacy, distance, and deliberate restraint. Although the two people remain deeply connected, they behave as though closeness must be carefully controlled. Bodily imagery emphasizes their awareness of one another, while domestic details place this tension within the ordinary spaces of shared life. At the same time, acrobatic imagery presents their avoidance as a difficult balancing act: not touching requires concentration, discipline, and a constant awareness of the other person’s presence. Their separation is therefore not a sign of indifference, but an effortful performance that reveals how powerful their attachment remains.

This tension is most clearly expressed through the image of their hearts. Though the hearts may beat irregularly, they remain synchronized, suggesting that the speakers share an emotional rhythm even when their outward actions imply distance. The apparent absence between them is not empty; it is charged with suppressed feeling. Likewise, their forbearance—the choice to hold back from contact—becomes evidence of intimacy because such restraint would be unnecessary without a strong desire for closeness. By presenting distance as something consciously maintained rather than naturally felt, the poem shows that separation cannot fully erase connection. Beneath silence, absence, and self-control, the two people continue to participate in a shared emotional life, their enduring attachment revealed by the pulse they cannot entirely conceal.
outputs.L5:
### Except You

The whole world seemed to be moving forward—trains leaving stations, birds crossing oceans, strangers turning corners toward new lives.

Everyone was going somewhere.

Except you.

You remained stuck between what had happened and what might have been, holding memories like keys to doors that no longer existed. But being stuck did not mean you were broken. Sometimes, stillness is where courage gathers.

One day, you loosened your grip on the past. You took a breath, then a step.

And the world moved with you.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal prose poem about emotional distance and intimacy between two people, using imagery of laundry, rare blood types, bedsheets, rib cages, magic tricks, acrobatics, and beating hearts.
counterfactuals.output:
We fold the laundry between us like a small, defeated country: your shirts on one border, my socks vanishing into another. The bedsheets come from the dryer warm as alibis, smelling of rain we never stood beneath together. You hold one corner. I hold the opposite. For a moment the whole room is a white flag neither of us intends to surrender.

You tell me your blood type is rare. I imagine tiny archivists inside you, labeling each red cell with gold thread, warning the world not to spill what cannot be easily replaced. I do not tell you mine. I want one mystery to remain useful.

At night, our rib cages lie side by side like two locked birdcages in a magician’s act. Your heart beats beneath the bars; mine answers from across the mattress, late by half a second. The distance is hardly anything—one bedsheet, one held breath, the thin blue vein of midnight—yet we perform elaborate acrobatics to cross it. You balance on the wire of my silence. I swing from the trapeze of your almost.

Sometimes you make a coin disappear behind my ear, though there is no coin and no ear, only your hand passing through the place where tenderness should have been. Still, I applaud. Still, you bow.

In the morning, we pull on our clothes, slightly smaller from the heat. Your sleeve remembers my wrist. My collar carries the shape of your mouth. We leave the bed unmade, its crumpled sheets resembling a map of two continents that once touched.

All day, beneath our separate ribs, the hearts continue their terrible trick: beating as if closeness were inevitable, beating as if distance were only another name for air.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a dense, lyrical paragraph exploring a relationship in which two lovers remain physically close but avoid touching, mistaking restraint and absence for acts of love.
counterfactuals.output: They lived within the same small weather, shoulder to shoulder beneath the lamp’s amber hush, sleeping on opposite shores of a bed that remembered the shape of their turning, and called this careful distance devotion. Each withheld the hand that might have crossed the dark; each mistook the ache of not reaching for proof of tenderness, as if love were best preserved by never being spent. In doorways they paused close enough to feel the warmth rise from one another’s skin, yet passed like ghosts trained in courtesy, offering silence where a mouth might have opened, absence where a body might have answered. Their restraint became a shrine they tended faithfully, polishing every unsaid word, arranging every avoided touch like flowers before an empty altar, until they could no longer tell whether they were protecting love from ruin or protecting themselves from love—and still, night after night, they lay inches apart, faithful to the beautiful wound between them.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an experimental prose poem titled “Double Bars of Depth” about two people whose hearts perform like trapeze artists inside one another’s rib cages.
counterfactuals.output:
# Double Bars of Depth

Inside your rib cage, my heart wears chalk on its hands.

Inside mine, yours is already airborne.

We have mistaken the body for a tent, the ribs for two curved ladders, the breath for an audience lifting its one white face. No net. No ground except the ground we keep inventing by falling toward it.

At midnight, our hearts trade trapezes. Mine swings from the blue bar of your grief; yours hooks its knees around the red bar of my wanting. They pass each other in the dark—small acrobats, sequined with blood—releasing exactly when release becomes impossible.

Catch, says the pulse.

Catch, says the hollow beneath it.

Sometimes your heart misses my heart and grabs a memory instead: the wet rope of a childhood, a door left open in winter, someone’s name still burning its little magnesium flare. Sometimes mine hangs by one hand from your silence, smiling as though terror were merely another form of applause.

We sleep side by side, but internally the distances are tremendous.

There: your heart somersaults through my sternum.

There: mine enters your chest like a question thrown across a ravine.

For one second—less—our hands meet.

The whole tent rises.

Then swing back, beloved. Swing back through the double bars of depth, through the animal rafters, through the dark that keeps making room for us. If we cannot hold forever, let us perfect the letting go: palm leaving palm, body becoming arc, faith becoming flight—

and each rib, struck softly,

ringing.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a contemporary prose poem in a fragmented, metaphor-heavy style. Include identical lots, dirty cuffs, clean shirts, walnut oil, fitted sheets, magician’s swords, and irregular heartbeats.
counterfactuals.output:
At the edge of town, identical lots hold their breath beneath identical rain. Houses rise like paused notifications, blue-lit and unfinished. Inside: fitted sheets snapped tight over the mattress, each corner disciplined, each dream resisting arrest.

You come home with dirty cuffs and a paper bag of clean shirts. The evening slips between them—evidence, alibi. In the kitchen, walnut oil gleams in its bottle, a small preserved sunset, too expensive to spill and too beautiful not to.

We speak in fragments. Rent. Weather. The bruise-colored future. Your phone vibrates like a trapped insect.

Somewhere, a magician lowers his swords into the box, smiling as if danger were only geometry. We know better. We have lived among magician’s swords: debt, silence, the sudden message after midnight. Still, the body volunteers for wonder.

Later, our irregular heartbeats tap through the dark—two faulty clocks arguing with eternity. Beyond the window, identical lots fill with fog. Every roof disappears. Every life, briefly, loses its outline.

You reach for me.

The trick is not survival.

The trick is making survival look like light.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an inseparable yet emotionally guarded pair through circus and anatomical metaphors, ending with the idea that each person must keep their fingers close to their own pulse.
counterfactuals.output: They moved like twin aerialists on a single wire, each trusting the other’s weight while hiding behind a painted grin. Their lives shared a rib cage of routines, but their hearts kept separate dressing rooms, curtains drawn. They could catch each other mid-fall, stitch silence to silence, and still never touch the tenderest wound. Love made them inseparable; fear kept them sealed. In the end, however tightly their hands were clasped, each had to keep their fingers close to their own pulse.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
